Stats NZ distributes release data through several generations of
information-release pages and attachment formats. `statsnzreleases` provides a
documented manifest of release families, with an explicit attachment and parser
rule for each supported workflow.

## What the manifest records

The complete manifest is available offline.  It records each family's support
status, expected publication frequency, title pattern, file-selection rule,
and a short note about the adapter.

```{r manifest}
manifest <- statsnzreleases::statsnz_releases(include_unsupported = TRUE)
manifest[, c(
  "release_id", "release_name", "frequency", "supported", "note"
)]
```

To list only families that the current package version can import:

```{r supported}
supported <- statsnzreleases::statsnz_releases(include_unsupported = FALSE)
supported[, c("release_id", "release_name", "frequency")]
```

The supported adapters cover Consumers Price Index, Gross Domestic
Product, Electronic Card Transactions, Retail Trade Survey, Balance of
Payments and International Investment Position, Labour Market Statistics, and
Overseas Merchandise Trade.  The manifest is the source of truth for the
installed version. Each live read validates the current release page and file
names before importing, which makes changed historical attachments visible as
typed errors.

## Attachment formats

The adapters select official attachments by family-specific rules:

- CSV release tables are parsed as character data first, then standardised
  with numeric values, periods, labels, and source columns.
- ZIP releases are inspected for safe CSV members before extraction.
- The Labour Market Statistics ZIP reader retains a curated, memory-aware set
  of quarterly HLFS, QES, and LCI headline series.
- Overseas Merchandise Trade workbooks are read through the package's curated
  monthly and quarterly headline/category tables.

Before a read, inspect the live page's attachments when needed.  This example
is intentionally conditional so vignette builds remain offline:

```{r inspect-live}
if (interactive()) {
  attachment_table <- statsnzreleases::statsnz_release_files(
    paste0(
      "https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/",
      "gross-domestic-product-march-2026-quarter/"
    )
  )
  attachment_table[, c("name", "title", "extension", "stated_size", "url")]
}
```

## Output contract

All supported readers return a tibble with class `statsnz_release_data`.
Common fields include:

```{r output-contract, results='asis'}
fields <- data.frame(
  field = c(
    "release_id", "release_name", "frequency", "series_reference",
    "series_label", "period", "period_date", "data_value",
    "data_value_raw", "source_file", "source_attachment_url"
  ),
  meaning = c(
    "Manifest identifier", "Human-readable family name", "Manifest frequency",
    "Exact source series reference", "Best available series description",
    "Original period label", "Parsed Date representation",
    "Numeric observation when conversion succeeds", "Original observation text",
    "Selected attachment name", "Official attachment URL"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(fields)
```

Additional source columns are retained when present, and missing standard
columns are represented as `NA`.  Duplicate series-period observations are
de-duplicated during standardisation.  `statsnz_provenance()` should be stored
alongside the table when a result is used outside the current R session.

## Release files and Aotearoa Data Explorer

Stats NZ is transitioning data from older dissemination tools into the
[Aotearoa Data Explorer](https://explore.data.stats.govt.nz/). The Data
Explorer and its API provide dataset discovery and custom table queries. The
[Stats NZ API Portal](https://portal.apis.stats.govt.nz/) requires users to
register, subscribe to the API product, and send a subscription key with API
requests.

`statsnzreleases` has a narrower release-file contract. It does not call the
Data Explorer catalogue or data endpoints and has no subscription-key option.
Its only JSON discovery request is to the separate, public Stats NZ website
release-calendar endpoint. It then reads the selected information-release page
and downloads the page's official CSV, ZIP, or XLSX attachments.

The same statistical topic may be present in both systems. Choose Data
Explorer for a custom query against a dataset available there. Choose
`statsnzreleases` when you need a supported release's published file, its page
context, the package's family-specific parser, or attachment-level hashes and
provenance. The package does not silently fall back to Data Explorer because
doing so could change the output schema, revision state, and source identity.

## Scope and limitations

Coverage is defined by the installed manifest; unsupported families are not
inferred, credentials are not required, and third-party mirrors are outside
scope. If Stats NZ removes or replaces the attachments for a supported family,
the existing typed page or attachment error makes that change visible rather
than changing access paths implicitly. For a new or migrated source, inspect
the manifest and email chartwellmacro@gmail.com with the official release family and current
access path so that coverage can be assessed explicitly.
